citations.text: Barzilai, S., & Chinn, C. A. (2018). On the goals of epistemic education: Promoting apt epistemic performance. Journal of the Learning Sciences, 27(3), 353-389.

en.general: The second-order part of fully apt performance, which Barzilai and Chinn take from Sosa: competence for assessing whether a judgment can be made reliably enough, based on awareness of how one's skills can be used successfully. It governs, for example, whether to form a belief or to withhold judgment.

examples: A reader holds off judging a health claim because they know they cannot judge the evidence themselves.
A reader defers to an expert on a question outside their own skills.
